section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the peace in the verse is the ultimate perfection of peace, where even former enemies become complete friends, surpassing the peace of Solomon's era and extending to the transformation of all opposition, including the serpent, to good, even higher than its original state before the sin.
section.t: And likewise, on the other hand,
that also the peace in this verse is
(not ordinary peace,
but rather)
the ultimate perfection of peace.
And as the Baal HaGeulah explains in the maamar,
that the true essence of the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is that those who were previously enemies and opponents "become complete lovers,"
for this matter is above even the peace that was in the days of Shlomo,
for the peace that was in the days of Shlomo is that all were nullified due to the revelation of light
(but they were not transformed into holiness),
and the true essence of peace
(that even the opponent is transformed into holiness)
will be in the future,
as it is written,
"For then I will turn to the peoples a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the L-rd, to serve Him with one accord,"
and likewise regarding animals — "and the wolf shall dwell with the lamb," etc.,
and even the serpent
(the viper and the adder)
will be transformed to good,
as it is written,
"He will also make peace with him" — this is the serpent,
and as it was at the beginning of creation
(before the sin of the Tree of Knowledge)
when there was a "great luminary."
And even more than this can be said,
that since every descent is for the sake of an ascent,
it must necessarily be said
that the refinement and ascent of the serpent in the future will be even higher than the level of the "great luminary" that existed before the descent.
And based on this, one must understand even more what is written, "He redeemed my soul in peace... for He drew me near,"
and yet nearness and peace in this verse are two opposites from one extreme to the other,
and how can it be "He redeemed my soul in peace... for He drew me near"?

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in the service of prayer, there are two aspects—nearness (through battle) and peace—corresponding to the loves of "with all your heart" (Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah) and "with all your soul" (Chayah) which involve struggle, while the love of "with all your might" (Yechidah) brings true peace by utterly nullifying the opposing side.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained in the maamar of the Baal HaGeulah,
that the two matters of nearness and peace exist in the service of prayer.
And to note,
that in many places
it is explained that the refinement of prayer is through the way of war,
"the time of prayer is a time of battle,"
and refinement through the way of rest
(peace)
is through the occupation with Torah.
But in this discourse of the Baal HaGeulah it is explained,
that also in the service of prayer there are both matters.
The love
of "with all your heart,"
which is from the aspect of Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah,
even though through this love he also causes that the Nefesh HaBahamis will also have love for G-d,
"with all your heart, with both your inclinations,"
nevertheless,
since the love of "with all your heart" is from comprehension and understanding
(that Elokus is good),
and since intellect is an aspect of pnimi
(which becomes invested in the thing it affects),
it is therefore understood that the action of the Nefesh HaElokis upon the Nefesh HaBahamis, that it love G-d, is through the Nefesh HaElokis becoming invested in the Nefesh HaBahamis,
for the contemplation of the Nefesh HaElokis must be about such matters and in a manner that the Nefesh HaBahamis can also grasp,
this investment
(that the Nefesh HaElokis becomes invested in the Nefesh HaBahamis)
is a matter of war.
And also the love of "with all your soul,"
which is from the aspect of Chayah,
although Chayah is an aspect of makif,
and the refinement of the Nefesh HaBahamis through this love is
(not through the way of investment,
but rather)
that from the intensity of the will of the Nefesh HaElokis
(a will that is above reason)
the wills of the Nefesh HaBahamis are automatically nullified,
nevertheless,
since the nullification of the wills of the Nefesh HaBahamis is only from the overpowering of the will of the Nefesh HaElokis,
meaning that even now the Nefesh HaBahamis has alien wills in concealment, but due to the overpowering of the will of the Nefesh HaElokis they do not come into actuality,
therefore this is included in the service of refinement through the way of war.
And the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is in the love of "with all your might,"
which is from the aspect of Yechidah.
For since the aspect of Yechidah has no opposite counterpart,
"the slightest reflection of it they do not have,"
therefore,
when the aspect of Yechidah is revealed,
the opposite side is nullified.
For the aspect of Chayah,
since it has an opposite counterpart,
therefore the revelation of the aspect of Chayah does not negate and nullify the alien wills of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
and it is only through the way of overpowering,
that the will for Elokus
(from the aspect of Chayah)
overpowers the wills of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
and in order for there to be a nullification of the wills of the Nefesh HaBahamis, it is through the revelation of Yechidah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section clarifies that the love of "with all your might" (Yechidah) uniquely involves self-sacrifice not as a choice but as an inability to be separated from G-d, which is the true nullification that completely eliminates the opposing side.
section.t: And one can connect this with the well-known concept
regarding the power of self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh) in every Jew
(for the power of self-sacrifice is from the aspect of Yechidah),
that his sacrificing his soul so as not to be separated, G-d forbid, from His Oneness, is not from his will
(meaning that it could be otherwise but he chooses this way),
but rather because he is unable to be separated, G-d forbid, from His Oneness.
And based on this, one can explain what is explained in many places,
that the love of "with all your might" is the matter of self-sacrifice.
For at first glance it is not understood,
for also the love of "with all your heart" and "with all your soul" seemingly obligate the matter of self-sacrifice,
for when one loves G-d with all his heart, and certainly when his love for G-d is with all his soul, he will surely sacrifice his soul for Him,
and what is the superiority and novelty in the love of "with all your might"?
And the explanation of this is,
that the self-sacrifice that comes from the love of "with all your heart" and "with all your soul" is in a manner that he wants to sacrifice his soul for G-d
(in the love of "with all your heart,"
Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah — a will based on reason and understanding,
and in the love of "with all your soul,"
Chayah — a will above reason),
in contrast, the self-sacrifice that comes from the love of "with all your might,"
Yechidah,
is in a manner that he is unable to be separated, G-d forbid.
And this is that the matter of self-sacrifice is in the love of "with all your might,"
for self-sacrifice is the matter of nullification,
and the true essence of nullification is when the self-sacrifice is not from his will
(existence)
but rather from the Elokus.
And it can be said,
that this is also one of the explanations in this, that the nullification of the alien wills of the Nefesh HaBahamis is specifically through the love of "with all your might,"
for the love of "with all your heart" and "with all your soul,"
since from this love there is a possibility not to sacrifice his soul
(and that he does sacrifice his soul is only from his will),
this proves that the existence of the opposite side still remains.
And the nullification of the opposite side
(complete nullification)
is through the love of "with all your might,"
for from this love it is impossible to be otherwise, G-d forbid.
